answer: At the knoll, every falcon must be anchored to a separate branch. One gale is one unit of capital burned by one branch for one other branch's falcon, and a branch cannot reuse a gale. To admit a new falcon, the knoll requires a gale from every existing branch for it, plus a gale from its branch for each existing falcon. The kth falcon costs 2k-2 gale, so n clones cost n(n-1) gale; batch clones still pay the final branch count because each ordered pair burns separately. Call this cross-branch capital quorum. It breaks if a branch can use one gale for another falcon.
